title: Replace All ?'s to Avoid Consecutive Repeating Characters
statement:
The string `s` is made of lowercase English letters and `'?'` marks. Swap every `'?'` for a lowercase letter so that no two neighbouring characters of the resulting string are the same, and return that string. Letters already in `s` must stay as they are.

The input guarantees that no two adjacent characters of `s` are the same letter (adjacent `'?'` marks are allowed), so a valid result always exists. When several results are valid, any one of them is accepted.
constraints: s contains only lowercase English letters and '?'
No two adjacent characters of s are the same letter
notes:
## Intuition

Each `'?'` only has to differ from its two neighbours, so it is blocked by at most two letters. Among the three letters `a`, `b`, `c`, at least one is always free. Filling left to right means the left neighbour is already final, and the right neighbour is either a fixed letter or another `'?'`, which cannot clash with a letter and will itself be chosen to avoid ours. A search over all 26 letters per mark would also work but is pointless.

## Approach

1. Copy `s` into an array `chars` so single characters can be replaced.
2. Walk the positions from left to right and skip every real letter.
3. For a `'?'`, read `left` (already filled, or empty at the start) and `right` (the next character, or empty at the end).
4. Put the first of `a`, `b`, `c` that equals neither `left` nor `right` into `chars[i]`.
5. Join `chars` back into a string.

## Example 1, step by step

`s = "?zs"`. At `i = 0` the mark has `left = ""` and `right = "z"`; `a` differs from both, so `chars` becomes `a z s`. Positions 1 and 2 are letters and are skipped. The result is `"azs"`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): each position is visited once and tries at most three letters.
- Space: O(n) for the character array (strings are immutable in JavaScript).

## Pitfalls

- Compare with the **replaced** left neighbour, not the original `'?'`, or `"??"` can become `"aa"`.
- Check both neighbours; looking only to the left fails on `"?a"`.
- Guard the ends of the string so `chars[-1]` and `chars[n]` are not treated as letters.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `chars` | the string as an editable array of characters |
| `i` | the position being processed |
| `left`, `right` | the neighbouring characters of position `i` (empty past an end) |
| `letter` | the candidate replacement being tried |

narration.4: Visit every position from left to right.
